content.text: {"persuasion":"PERSUADED","support_scope":"FULL","rationale":"The BOOK ENTRY defines 'the truth' as God's law, the standard. Its lead proof text, Psalm 119:142 KJV, states this identification verbatim: 'thy law is the truth' — not 'thy law is true,' but a definite predicate identification. John 17:17 ('thy word is truth'), quoted in the supporting chapter, gives an independent second witness, and 2 John 4 (walking 'in truth') sits in a letter whose immediate continuation defines that walk as walking 'after his commandments' (2 John 6), which corroborates the law-as-truth reading rather than a bare Christological one. The strongest counter — that 'the truth' is exclusively the person of Christ (John 14:6), with John 1:17 setting law against truth — cannot account for Psalm 119:142 without weakening its explicit copula into a mere quality, and it must also soften John 17:17. The book's reading, by contrast, absorbs John 14:6 without strain: the chapter argues Christ is the truth precisely as the law embodied, so the personal and the legal referents converge rather than conflict. Notably, the common interpretation itself lists 'truth as God's word' as a dominant reading; the entry's divergence is one of emphasis and precision (the standard) rather than a denial of the consensus's material content. No supplied text is better explained by the counter than by the entry, so the entry stands as the best-supported explanation of the cited evidence.","book_core_identification":"'The truth,' used with the definite article as a scriptural symbol, refers to God's law/word — the divine standard or measure by which everything else is judged (Ps 119:142; John 17:17).","book_secondary_elaborations":["The appositive gloss 'the standard' — i.e., the truth is not merely accurate statement but God's own measure against which all else is weighed."],"unsupported_glossary_assertions":[],"chapter_only_objections":["The claim that Hebrews 10:20 prosphatos means 'freshly slain' rather than 'new' is a contested etymological argument (the word had lost its slaughter sense in Koine usage) and is not asserted in the glossary entry.","The identification of the flaming sword of Genesis 3:24 with 'the sword of the Spirit, the word of God' (Eph 6:17) is a typological leap made only in the chapter.","The footnote claim that 'the gospel' is the message Jesus taught rather than the message about Him is a chapter-level (and separate-chapter) thesis, not part of this entry.","The lion/beast/highway symbolic derivations (Dan 7:23; Prov 28:15; Isa 35:8-9) are chapter-only supporting material.","The reading of John 14:6's 'unto the Father' as pointedly excluding 'to heaven' is a chapter-level interpretive aside."],"strongest_counter_interpretation":"The mainstream Christological reading: 'the truth' is first and foremost Jesus Christ in person (John 14:6; John 1:14, 17; Eph 4:21), not the Mosaic law; indeed John 1:17 appears to contrast the two — 'the law was given by Moses, but grace and truth came by Jesus Christ' — so defining the truth as 'God's law' allegedly inverts the Johannine emphasis and reduces a personal, relational reality to a legal code.","counter_core_identification":"'The truth' is the self-revelation of God in the person of Jesus Christ, communicated by the Spirit and extended to the gospel message, rather than the law as a standard.","counter_relation_to_book_core":"SAME_CORE_BROADER","material_core_denial":"In its strongest exclusive form the counter denies that 'the truth' refers to God's law as the standard, insisting the referent is the person of Christ as opposed to a body of commandment; but in its ordinary layered form (as the common interpretation itself concedes, listing 'truth as God's word' among dominant readings) it includes the entry's referent as one strand, and the chapter's synthesis — Christ as the Torah embodied — makes both true of the same referent.","counter_case":["John 14:6 predicates 'the truth' of a person, not a text or code.","John 1:17 appears to set the law given by Moses over against the grace and truth that came by Jesus Christ.","Ephesians 4:21 says 'the truth is in Jesus,' anchoring truth in the person.","The Spirit is called 'the Spirit of truth' and even 'the truth' (1 John 5:6), suggesting a personal rather than legal referent.","Hebrew emet often denotes covenant faithfulness (Exod 34:6), not a legal standard."],"book_explanatory_advantages":["Psalm 119:142 states the entry's identification verbatim in the cited KJV text: 'thy law is the truth' — a definite identification the counter must dilute into a mere attribute.","John 17:17 ('thy word is truth') supplies a second, independent explicit predication of truth of God's word, matching the two-witness standard the book's method requires.","2 John 4's 'walking in truth' is immediately glossed by 2 John 6 as walking after His commandments, tying the entry's second proof text to the law-as-standard reading.","The entry's reading explains why 'truth' takes the definite article and functions as a measure ('sanctify them through thy truth') — a standard sanctifies; a bare fact does not.","The book's synthesis absorbs the Christological data rather than contradicting it: John 14:6 is read as the standard embodied in a person, so 'the truth is Christ' and 'the truth is God's law' converge instead of competing.","The entry coheres with the common interpretation's own dominant alternative (truth as God's word/Scripture), so it diverges only by sharpening the referent to 'the standard,' not by opposing consensus texts."],"counter_explanatory_advantages":["John 14:6 and Ephesians 4:21 are most naturally read as personal predications, which the counter takes at face value without the intermediate 'law embodied' step.","John 1:17's rhetorical contrast between law and grace-and-truth is prima facie friendlier to the counter.","The counter better foregrounds the pneumatological texts (John 16:13; 1 John 5:6)."],"evidence_book_core_cannot_explain":[],"comparative_winner":"BOOK","decisive_sources":["Psalm 119:142 KJV — 'thy law is the truth' (explicit identification, the entry's printed proof text)","John 17:17 — 'thy word is truth' (independent second witness quoted in the supporting chapter)","2 John 4 read with 2 John 6 — truth walked in is defined as walking after His commandments","Proverbs 6:23 (quoted in the chapter) — commandment, law, and 'way of life' strung on one thread, showing truth functioning as the standard within the way/truth/life triad"],"unresolved_objections":["John 1:17's law-versus-truth contrast is answered plausibly (contrast of mediation, not identity) but not from a text supplied in the evidence bundle.","Whether 'the standard' fully captures Hebrew emet's connotation of faithfulness/reliability in Psalm 119:142 is a lexical nuance the entry does not address, though it does not defeat the explicit predication."],"confidence":"high"}
